display_name: Sepsis Secondary to Urinary Tract Infection

patient_profile.name: Patient B
patient_profile.presenting_complaint: brought in confused, fever, and weakness for 1 day

hidden_ground_truth.diagnosis: Sepsis secondary to urosepsis (E. coli UTI)
hidden_ground_truth.correct_first_line_treatment: IV fluids, blood cultures + urine culture BEFORE antibiotics, empiric broad-spectrum IV antibiotics within 1 hour, monitor lactate
red_herrings: mild dehydration framed as sole cause of confusion

on_direct_questioning.urinary_symptoms: dysuria and urgency for 3 days prior, patient forgot to mention initially

lab_results.urinalysis: positive leukocyte esterase, positive nitrites, many bacteria
lab_results.blood_cultures: pending at time of initial workup, later grows E. coli
lab_results.renal_function: creatinine mildly elevated from baseline (acute kidney injury, likely prerenal)

progression_rules.if_untreated_or_delayed: progresses to septic shock (hypotension refractory to fluids, worsening lactate, organ dysfunction) within hours
progression_rules.if_correct_treatment: rapid stabilization within 24-48 hours with fluids + appropriate antibiotics + source control
progression_rules.if_incorrect_or_unnecessary_treatment: e.g. antibiotics delayed for imaging, or narrow-spectrum antibiotic chosen empirically before culture data, worsens trajectory
progression_rules.if_unnecessary_invasive_test_ordered: simulate normal/expected result, note added delay in scoring
